summary: A finished international standard for immersive sound in virtual and augmented spaces, published on 2025-11-03 as edition 1.0. It models sound sources together with the space around them, covering reverberation, early reflections, occlusion, bending of sound around edges and pitch shift from movement, with the listener free to both turn and walk, and it carries all of that in a compressed stream. Its own listening test, run across six laboratories and reported in January 2026, placed it in the excellent band at a middle score of 84 out of 100, so saying nobody is working on spatial sound is false. Be clear about the evidence here: the normative text is sold, not published, and we did not read it. Every row below rests on the publisher's catalogue record, the group's own standard page, its own white paper and its own test report, so every row is marked reported rather than verified. The trap worth taking to a working group is that it needs the scene geometry a second time, in its own encoder input format, so a world that already describes its walls for pictures must describe them again for sound.

coverage.note: Sound is placed in the scene as objects with position and orientation, and sources may also carry a size and shape, from a piano up to a forest. Channel beds and ambisonic fields are carried too.

sources.title: MPEG-I: Immersive Audio, official MPEG standard page
sources.quote: The scenes consist of audio objects and acoustic properties of the room including the simulation of acoustics like reverberation, early reflections, occlusion, diffraction and Doppler-shift.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-4:2025 catalogue record, Information technology - Coded representation of immersive media - Part 4: MPEG-I immersive audio
sources.quote: supports the real-time interactive rendering of an immersive virtual or augmented reality audio presentation while permitting the user to have 6DoF movement in the audio scene

coverage.note: The listener can walk as well as turn, which is the step past the earlier three-axis standard. Output is either to headphones as a two-ear mix or to a loudspeaker rig from six up to twenty-four channels.

sources.title: MPEG-I: Immersive Audio, official MPEG standard page
sources.quote: In addition to the 3DoF head movements (yaw, pitch and roll), which had already been supported by MPEG-H 3D Audio, the listener can now move within the acoustic scene (x,y,z).

coverage.note: Rooms are first-class: each acoustic environment has its own late reverberation, early reflections are computed from the transmitted geometry, and openings between rooms pass sound from one to the next. A separate listening space description carries the shape and surfaces of the real room the listener is standing in.

sources.title: MPEG-I: Immersive Audio, official MPEG standard page
sources.quote: The scenes consist of audio objects and acoustic properties of the room including the simulation of acoustics like reverberation, early reflections, occlusion, diffraction and Doppler-shift.

coverage.note: Blocking and part-blocking of sound by geometry are separate named stages of the renderer, and bending around an edge is handled alongside them so a hidden source is still heard from the right direction.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: The Occlusion stage provides occlusion information with respect to a direct path from source to user.

coverage.note: The standard defines the coded form itself, sized for narrow links, and works either as a file or as a live stream.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-4:2025 catalogue record, Information technology - Coded representation of immersive media - Part 4: MPEG-I immersive audio
sources.quote: It defines metadata to support this rendering and a bitstream syntax that enables efficient storage and streaming of immersive audio content.

coverage.note: It defines the stream and how the six-axis metadata is packed alongside the coded audio, using three new packet types in the older audio stream format. It does not define the network protocol that carries those packets, and it carries no video.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: The MPEG-I immersive audio bitstream transport relies on MHAS (MPEG-H Audio Stream), by introducing three new packet types to carry the 6DoF metadata alongside the MPEG-H 3D audio signal assets.

coverage.note: It can render a talker's voice into the scene once that voice has arrived, which is listed as a social use case. It defines nothing about getting live voice from one participant to another: no capture, no codec choice for speech, no session and no mixing rules. This is the gap next to an otherwise complete audio standard.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: enabling acoustic interaction with the scene supporting e.g. virtual meetings

coverage.note: It carries its own copy of the scene shape, as boxes, meshes or solid blocks, because the renderer needs surfaces to reflect and bend sound off. What is missing is any tie to the visual asset: this is an acoustic description authored separately, so the same room gets described twice, once for pictures and once for sound.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: a dedicated scene description file format has been developed called Encoder Input Format (EIF) that holds definitions for e.g. sources and their positions, scene geometry (primitives, meshes or voxels), transforms, material acoustic coefficients, etc.

coverage.note: Worth stating so nobody double-counts it. The standard does define surface materials, but they are sound properties: how much energy a surface passes, reflects, couples and soaks up, by frequency. There is no friction, no bounce and nothing a contact solver could use.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: These materials are characterized by parameters describing transmitted, reflected, coupled and absorbed audio energy parts.

coverage.note: A scene can name a region and fire a change when the listener enters it. What is missing is everything outside sound: the change may only alter the acoustic scene, so this is not a general rule engine and will not drive world logic.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: Conditional scene updates define a specific condition that triggers the scene update.

coverage.note: For augmented use it places virtual sound content into the real room the listener occupies, using the measured room description. What is missing is anything shared or lasting: no anchor identifier, no storage, nothing that another device or a later session could reuse.

sources.title: White Paper on MPEG-I Immersive Audio, ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 29/AG 03 N150
sources.quote: an anchor mechanism is used for placing scene content in appropriate positions in the listening space

coverage.note: Hearing needs are handled inside the renderer rather than bolted on afterwards: a listener can ask for less late reverberation or for sources away from where they are looking to be quietened. What is missing is portability. The published description has those choices arriving through a local interface, and says nothing about a format that would carry them from one service to the next.

coverage.note: MPEG-I Immersive Audio is the sound half of the same family: sources, room acoustics and a listener who can walk, and making a whole three-dimensional place from a description or a picture is not an act it performs or specifies.

coverage.note: A listener can join a running broadcast because the scene configuration packet is repeated through the stream and a sync packet precedes it. Nothing covers authentication or admission.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), 5.1 Overview
sources.quote: To sync to the broadcast stream an MHAS sync packet PACTYP_SYNC shall be inserted before each mpegiSceneConfig() packet.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), 5.1 Overview

coverage.note: Source and listener positions can change over time through timed and live updates, and started trajectories are interpolated. The only rule is linear interpolation, and there is no format for a recorded series of poses.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), scene controller, update
sources.quote: Interpolated updates: the scene controller evaluates previously received and started metadata trajectories and updates the scene state accordingly.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), scene controller, update
sources.quote: Temporal interpolations can be triggered by pre-defined, location-based or local updates when the update contains a duration and are always linear interpolations.

coverage.note: Each audio element can point to one parent transform or anchor, and an anchor takes its position from the listener-space description. Transforms cannot nest, so the stream carries single links, not longer chains or graphs.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), scene controller, transform
sources.quote: Transforms can be used in the bitstream to group other SOs into a separate relative coordinate system, and to represent ARAnchors from the LSI.

sources.title: Text of ISO/IEC FDIS 23090-4 MPEG-I immersive audio (final draft, ed.1, 2025-03-25), payload semantics, primitives()
sources.quote: primitiveHasAnchor This flag indicates if this primitive's spatial transform is an anchor. If FALSE, then the parent is a regular transform.

coverage.note: Who may do what is not a question for a standard that renders and streams sound.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-4:2025 catalogue record, Information technology - Coded representation of immersive media - Part 4: MPEG-I immersive audio
sources.quote: This document specifies technology that supports the real-time interactive rendering of an immersive virtual or augmented reality audio presentation while permitting the user to have 6DoF movement in the audio scene. It defines metadata to support this rendering and a bitstream syntax that enables efficient storage and streaming of immersive audio content.

coverage.note: Identifiers for people, agents or things are outside a standard for rendering and streaming sound; the only identifiers here name scene entities.
